authority.note: Stress priority and test results inform later judgment; neither can decide a swap or approval alone.

execution_policy.goldfish_threshold: read declared readiness metrics only; never relabel as multiplayer win probability
execution_policy.judgment_prompt: requires later red-team/judgment review; no fake simulator substitute
execution_policy.mechanic_module: use the relevant Step-E bounded module; preserve its declared assumptions and category separation
execution_policy.simulator_scenario: paired deterministic perturbation against same-seed baseline

items.question: Repeated commander removal and tax recovery.
Temporary pressure on the commander's most-demanded color.
Can the deck rebuild after repeated removal across multiple permanent types?
Can combat/targeting-dependent routes function through pillowfort or must the deck pivot?
Can the deck progress through token stalls and clogged combat?
Does the deck have credible answers/recovery when key artifacts/enchantments are removed or opposing permanents must be answered?

limitations: Priority weights allocate review/testing attention and are never multiplied by outcomes into a deck score.
B5 and B4 intentionally emphasize different failure modes.
Opponent-facing mechanics use only bounded Step-E proxies where implemented.
Judgment-only stresses remain judgment-only until a defensible model exists.
No stress result can approve a deck or independently decide a swap.
